messages:
incident-bot: Pager: 3xx spike + KV cache memory growth on us-west-2. Affected service: inference-runtime. Severity: P1. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/1856002345 :rotating_light:
maya (oncall): ack, looking now. seeing sustained 3xxs from batch worker pool, errors are `kv-cache::evict_fail` and `batch: submit_timeout` in logs.
raj (eng-runtime): on it — starting quick heap check on the kvcache VM group. any customer reports?
maya (oncall): tom, can you check support queue for any customer-facing alerts?
tom (customer-ops): had 1 complain via email from Acme.mini (low volume) reporting slow responses. No major outages reported by other customers yet.
lina (sre): I see an amplification loop in metrics: continuous batching size is increasing for a subset of keys causing KV cache entries to grow -> GC thrash. suspect config change rolled @ 02:15 UTC to sampling policy.
raj (eng-runtime): confirming: recent feature-flag rollout `batch.dynamic_sampling=true` pushed from canary to 50% at 02:12. Canary logs show batch window grew 3x -> KV insert rate spike.
maya (oncall): okay isolate: can we toggle the flag back to stable? prefer per-customer override for Acme first and global if needed.
raj (eng-runtime): preparing rollback. quick plan: 1) flip `batch.dynamic_sampling` off for production via flag toggle to 0% canary 2) enable per-customer override for Acme to immediate=stable.
ops-bot: Command acknowledged: flagctl set batch.dynamic_sampling 0% --env=prod --actor=maya. Request ID: fd3a2
ops-bot: Command acknowledged: per-customer override set customer=Acme.mini batch.window=default --actor=raj. Request ID: 9c1b8
maya (oncall): flipping global back now, doing a staged ramp down (50 -> 25 -> 0) to avoid sudden load.
raj (eng-runtime): logs: rolling flag back at 02:23, canary group size decreasing. KV insert rate dropping for most hosts.
lina (sre): seeing reduced mem pressure on KV nodes in us-west-2, GC pauses falling. error rate dropping from 7% -> 1.2% across the pool.
tom (customer-ops): Acme.mini reports improvement in response times. they were on a single shard that got the worst of the blowup.
maya (oncall): good. decision: keep per-customer override for Acme.mini pinned to stable for 24h and continue global at 0% until we have root cause.
raj (eng-runtime): agreed. start deeper postmortem: collect profile traces from 01:50-02:30 window, export KV cache stats, and diff kernel selection logs.
lina (sre): I'll open an incident ticket with timeline and assign `investigate-cache-sampling` to eng-runtime + SRE.
maya (oncall): handoff to raj for next shift. raj, you're primary owner for mitigation and RCA. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then hand to next oncall.
raj (eng-runtime): taking ownership. quick patch plan: revert sampling logic, add guard to limit batch window growth per key, and add a safety circuit breaker to prevent >X inserts/sec per host.
ops-bot: Alert: config-change requires PR + canary. Recommend hotpatch via feature-flag rollback instead of code PR to restore stability.
maya (oncall): noted. we'll do flag rollback as short term then ship code fix.
tom (customer-ops): prepping a short customer message for impacted tenants: ETA 30m for full recovery, no data loss, mitigation applied.
raj (eng-runtime): running health-checks across regions. us-east looks fine, us-west degraded earlier but now stabilizing.
lina (sre): SLO impact calc: estimated 1.8% latency SLO burn for the 40m window. will add to incident doc.
maya (oncall): any objections to keeping per-customer overrides open for a while? want to avoid flip-flopping if the fix regresses.
raj (eng-runtime): keep overrides pinned for Acme.mini and a second affected tenant `beta-inc`. I'll create per-customer flags: `override.batch.window=default` for both.
ops-bot: per-customer flags active: Acme.mini, beta-inc. IDs: pfx-7a, pfx-7b.
maya (oncall): thanks team. continuing monitoring. if error rate creeps >3% we escalate to incident postmortem call.
raj (eng-runtime): adding a lightweight metric alarm to watch KV insertion rate per-host and global batching growth. rule: alert if >2000 inserts/sec sustained 2m.
lina (sre): next steps for RCA: 1) confirm which kernel selection path caused the growth 2) reproduce locally with traced workload 3) add a circuit breaker in runtime to cap per-key window.
maya (oncall): handing-off complete. last check: error rate at 0.9%, KV mem usage trending down. last_message_ts=1856004510
incident-bot: Incident 1856002345 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
